findings.title: Pool configure callback re-enters DatabaseWrapper when assume_role is set
findings.suggested_fix: In the module-level ensure_role(), stop calling ops.compose_sql() (it routes through the Django wrapper's cursor). Compose on the raw connection instead, e.g. for psycopg 3 `sql = Database.ClientCursor(connection).mogrify("SET ROLE %s", [role_name])` and for psycopg2 `sql = cursor.mogrify("SET ROLE %s", [role_name]).decode()`, then `cursor.execute(sql)`. Add a test that connects with both pool and assume_role set.

findings.title: New atomic-block guard permanently blocks reconnect when autocommit is off
findings.suggested_fix: Clear the stale flag when the outermost block exits with autocommit disabled, in django/db/transaction.py Atomic.__exit__: in the `elif not connection.savepoint_ids and not connection.commit_on_exit:` branch set `connection.in_atomic_block = False` in both cases (keep `connection.connection = None` when closed_in_transaction). That leaves the guard effective only while the block is really active. Add a non-autocommit test: set_autocommit(False); with atomic(): connection.close(); then run a query.

findings.title: Alias-keyed pool keeps stale connection params after settings_dict changes

Assumption: closing is safe in the creating process; for a forked worker the inherited entry should be discarded from _connection_pools without closing the parent's sockets. Alternatively compare the cached pool's kwargs with get_connection_params() in the pool property and rebuild on mismatch.

findings.title: Empty pool options dict silently disables pooling
findings.suggested_fix: Use an explicit check in the pool property (and the same condition in get_connection_params and features.django_test_skips): `if self.alias == NO_DB_ALIAS or pool_options is None or pool_options is False: return None`.
findings.first_evidence: django/db/backends/postgresql/base.py:205 -- if self.alias == NO_DB_ALIAS or not pool_options:

residual_risks: No PostgreSQL server was available, so the pooled paths (getconn/putconn, the pool + assume_role hang, closing inside an atomic block with a pool) were traced from source and checked with mocks only, not run end to end.

Fork-based parallel test workers inherit the class-level DatabaseWrapper._connection_pools dict; if the parent holds an open pool at fork time the workers would share its sockets and its database name. Whether the parent has a live pool at that point was not established.

Pool options are splatted after fixed keyword arguments (ConnectionPool(kwargs=..., open=False, configure=..., check=..., **pool_options)), so a user dict containing kwargs, open, configure or check raises TypeError 'got multiple values for keyword argument' (observed for {'check': None}) rather than a configuration error.

close_pool() and ensure_timezone() evaluate the pool property, which builds a new ConnectionPool only to close it and can raise ImproperlyConfigured from the setting_changed handler; concurrent close_pool() calls for one alias can race on `del self._connection_pools[self.alias]`. Only test-time paths call these today.
testing_gaps: No test connects with both OPTIONS['pool'] and OPTIONS['assume_role'] set; test_connect_role explicitly uses a non-pooled connection.

No test closes a connection inside an atomic block with autocommit disabled and then reuses the connection after the block; the new guard is only tested by setting in_atomic_block/closed_in_transaction by hand.
No test covers a pool that already exists when create_test_db()/setup_worker_connection() switch settings_dict['NAME'].

findings.title: Atomic guard bricks AUTOCOMMIT=False connections; test fakes state
findings.suggested_fix: In django/db/transaction.py Atomic.__exit__ (lines 309-313, the 'Outermost block exit when autocommit was disabled' branch), also set connection.in_atomic_block = False when connection.closed_in_transaction is true (i.e. set connection.connection = None in that case and reset in_atomic_block unconditionally). Verified on a scratch copy of the reviewed tree: the reproduction then reconnects after the block while the guard still fires inside the block. Add coverage: (1) in tests/transactions/tests.py NonAutocommitTests, a test doing `with transaction.atomic(): connection.close()` followed by an ORM query that must succeed (mirror the existing test_atomic_prevents_queries_in_broken_transaction_after_client_close at tests/transactions/tests.py:375, including its skipUnlessDBFeature('test_db_allows_multiple_connections')); (2) a backend-agnostic test of the guard in tests/backends/base/test_base.py instead of only the psycopg3-gated one. Assumption: reconnecting after the outermost atomic block exits is the intended contract, as the comment at django/db/backends/base/base.py:349-351 ('The next connect() will reset the transaction state anyway') states.

findings.title: Pooled close-inside-atomic lifecycle has no real test
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite test_cannot_open_new_connection_in_atomic_block to produce the state through the lifecycle instead of assigning it: build the pooled wrapper as today (no_pool_connection(alias='default_pool') with OPTIONS['pool'] = True), register it with `connections['default_pool'] = new_connection`, then `with transaction.atomic(using='default_pool'): new_connection.close()`, assert `new_connection.connection is None`, and assert `new_connection.cursor()` raises ProgrammingError with the guard message inside the block; after the block assert a `SELECT 1` succeeds again. Clean up in finally with new_connection.close(), new_connection.close_pool() and `del connections['default_pool']`. Assumption: registering a temporary alias on the connection handler is acceptable in this test module; if not, call new_connection.connect(), set only in_atomic_block = True, and let new_connection.close() produce closed_in_transaction and the None connection before asserting the guard.

findings.title: Docs say psycopg2 ignores pool; code and test raise
findings.suggested_fix: Change docs/ref/databases.txt:270-271 to state that the option requires psycopg[pool] or psycopg-pool and is not supported with psycopg2 (ImproperlyConfigured is raised), and rename the test at tests/backends/postgresql/tests.py:349 to test_connect_pool_setting_raises_for_psycopg2. Assumption: raising is the intended behavior because the implementation and the test assertion agree; if ignoring is intended instead, drop the raise at django/db/backends/postgresql/base.py:291-292, make the pool property return None when not is_psycopg3, and rewrite the test to assert a normal connection.

residual_risks: None of the new or modified PostgreSQL tests were executed: no PostgreSQL server is provisioned. Statements about which mutants the new tests would kill are by inspection plus offline mock-driven checks of the wrapper, not from running tests/backends/postgresql/tests.py.

No in-repo configuration runs the suite with OPTIONS['pool'] enabled (the only matches for 'pool' under .github, tox.ini, tests/runtests.py, tests/requirements and tests/backends are tests/backends/postgresql/tests.py and tests/requirements/postgres.txt). The pool-conditional django_test_skips in django/db/backends/postgresql/features.py and the ensure_timezone()/_close() 'workaround for tests' paths imply an out-of-tree pooled CI run that I could not see; whether pooled mode is exercised by the wider suite depends on it.

test_connect_pool (tests/backends/postgresql/tests.py:241-245) creates its pool with min_size 0 and timeout 0.1, and DatabaseWrapper.get_new_connection() calls pool.getconn() with no per-call timeout, so the same 100 ms real-time budget that makes the third checkout fail also bounds establishing and configuring each brand-new server connection (connect, authentication, SET TIME ZONE). On a loaded or remote database the first get_connection() can raise PoolTimeout spuriously. ConnectionPool.timeout is a public attribute, so the pool could be created with the default timeout and lowered only around the assertRaises(PoolTimeout). Frequency not measurable here.

test_pooling_health_checks (tests/backends/postgresql/tests.py:318, 324) asserts on psycopg_pool's private ConnectionPool._check attribute. It exists in the installed psycopg_pool 3.3.3 (pool.py:75), but a rename upstream would break the test without any Django behavior change.
testing_gaps: DatabaseWrapper.close_if_health_check_failed() (django/db/backends/postgresql/base.py:501-505) is covered only by skipping two base health-check tests under pooling; no test asserts that a pooled wrapper with CONN_HEALTH_CHECKS enabled does not call is_usable(). This is testable without a server (offline check with a mocked connection and patched is_usable confirmed the bypass).

The psycopg_pool ImportError path (django/db/backends/postgresql/base.py:217-222, 'Error loading psycopg_pool module') has no test; patching sys.modules['psycopg_pool'] to None reproduces it offline and would pin the message.

assume_role under pooling is untested: test_connect_role and every other option test were switched to no_pool_connection(), so the role half of _configure_connection() running as the pool's configure callback (and how a failing SET ROLE surfaces through the pool) is exercised only for time zones (test_connect_pool_with_timezone).

DatabaseWrapper.ensure_timezone() closing the pool (django/db/backends/postgresql/base.py:364) and _close() returning a connection to its original connection._pool after the alias's pool was replaced (base.py:392-395) have no focused test; test_connect_pool_with_timezone uses a wrapper that is not registered in django.db.connections, so the setting_changed handler never calls its ensure_timezone().

The close_pool() calls added to _clone_test_db() and the new _destroy_test_db() override in django/db/backends/postgresql/creation.py have no test; tests/backends/postgresql/test_creation.py is unchanged.

findings.title: Pool plus assume_role wedges: configure callback re-enters the pool
findings.suggested_fix: In the module-level ensure_role(), stop calling ops.compose_sql() (which goes through DatabaseWrapper.cursor()). Build the statement from the raw connection argument instead, e.g. for psycopg 3 `cursor.execute(ClientCursor(connection).mogrify("SET ROLE %s", [role_name]))` and for psycopg2 `cursor.execute(cursor.mogrify("SET ROLE %s", [role_name]))`, or use a server-side parameterised form parallel to set_time_zone_sql(): `cursor.execute("SELECT set_config('role', %s, false)", [role_name])`. Add a pooled test for assume_role (test_connect_role was switched to no_pool_connection(), so the pooled path is untested).

findings.title: Pool keyed by alias keeps serving the pre-test database
findings.suggested_fix: Invalidate the alias's pool whenever the wrapper's connection settings are rewritten: call self.connection.close_pool() right after NAME is reassigned in create_test_db() (base/creation.py:64-66, e.g. via a PostgreSQL DatabaseCreation hook), in set_as_test_mirror() and in setup_worker_connection(). In DatabaseWrapper._nodb_cursor()'s fallback, build the temporary wrapper with pooling disabled ("OPTIONS": {**self.settings_dict["OPTIONS"], "pool": False}) so it cannot register a pool under self.alias. More robust alternative: have the pool property compare the cached pool's kwargs with get_connection_params() and recreate the pool when they differ. Assumption: pools are meant to follow settings_dict changes the way non-pooled connections do.

findings.title: Docs say pool is ignored with psycopg2; code raises
findings.suggested_fix: Change docs/ref/databases.txt:270-271 to state that the option requires psycopg 3 with psycopg[pool]/psycopg-pool installed and raises ImproperlyConfigured with psycopg2, and rename the test to match (e.g. test_connect_pool_setting_requires_psycopg3).
findings.first_evidence: docs/ref/databases.txt:270-271 -- This option requires ``psycopg[pool]`` or :pypi:`psycopg-pool` to be installed and is ignored with ``psycopg2``.

residual_risks: Fail-fast is lost on the pooled path: with the database down or the pool exhausted (psycopg_pool defaults: min_size=max_size=4, timeout=30s, reconnect_timeout=300s), get_new_connection() blocks each caller for the pool timeout and then raises PoolTimeout; the underlying connect error is only logged at WARNING on the 'psycopg.pool' logger. The docs added here do not mention sizing or timeout, so 'pool': True on a server with more than 4 concurrent DB-using threads queues requests behind a 30s wait.

A pooled connection is returned only from DatabaseWrapper._close(); BaseDatabaseWrapper has no __del__, so a thread that uses the ORM outside the request cycle and exits without connection.close() permanently removes a slot from the pool (psycopg_pool getconn docstring: 'failing to do so will deplete the pool'), whereas the non-pooled path frees the server connection on garbage collection.

Fork safety not verified: _connection_pools is a class-level dict, psycopg_pool has no fork handling (no register_at_fork/pid check found in the installed 3.3.3 source), and connections.close_all() does not close pools. A pool opened before fork (preloading servers, the fork-based parallel test runner if the parent connects after the last clone) is inherited with idle sockets shared with the parent and no worker threads in the child.
Both P1 findings were reproduced against the real psycopg_pool with a stub connection_class because no PostgreSQL server is provisioned; they were not run against a live server.
testing_gaps: No test exercises OPTIONS['assume_role'] together with OPTIONS['pool']; test_connect_role was moved to no_pool_connection(), so the pool's configure callback path for SET ROLE is never run.

No test checks that a pooled alias follows a settings_dict['NAME'] change (create_test_db, set_as_test_mirror, setup_worker_connection, or the _nodb_cursor fallback wrapper); only the TIME_ZONE/USE_TZ change is covered via ensure_timezone().

findings.title: Pool plus assume_role deadlocks: configure callback re-enters the pool
findings.suggested_fix: In ensure_role(), stop using ops.compose_sql() (it calls mogrify(sql, params, <DatabaseWrapper>) -> wrapper.cursor()). Compose against the raw connection passed in, e.g. on psycopg 3 `sql = ClientCursor(connection).mogrify("SET ROLE %s", [role_name])` (psycopg2: `cursor.mogrify(...).decode()`), or execute `SELECT set_config('role', %s, false)` with the parameter, mirroring set_time_zone_sql(). Add a pooled assume_role test (test_connect_role was switched to no_pool_connection(), so the combination is untested).

findings.title: Stale pool survives test-DB NAME switch; tests hit real database
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the _clone_test_db handling in django/db/backends/postgresql/creation.py: override _create_test_db to end with `self.connection.close(); self.connection.close_pool()` (close first, because _close() evaluates self.pool and would lazily rebuild a pool with the old NAME), and override setup_worker_connection / set_as_test_mirror to call `self.connection.close_pool()` after super(). More robust alternative: make DatabaseWrapper.pool rebuild when get_connection_params() no longer matches the cached pool's kwargs (or key _connection_pools on alias plus dbname/host/port/user). Assumption: pre-setup DB access on the alias is the trigger; it is discouraged but common enough that Django warns about it.

findings.title: Base guard bricks non-autocommit wrapper after close() inside atomic
findings.suggested_fix: In Atomic.__exit__ (django/db/transaction.py:309-313, 'Outermost block exit when autocommit was disabled'), reset `connection.in_atomic_block = False` in the closed_in_transaction arm as well (after `connection.connection = None`), matching the autocommit-enabled branch where the flag is already False, so the guard only fires while a block is genuinely open. Add a regression test: set_autocommit(False); with atomic(): connection.close(); then run a query.
findings.first_evidence: django/db/backends/base/base.py:274 -- if self.in_atomic_block and self.closed_in_transaction:   (raises ProgrammingError before `self.connect()`)

findings.title: Docs say pool is ignored on psycopg2; code raises ImproperlyConfigured
findings.suggested_fix: Change the sentence in docs/ref/databases.txt to state that the option requires psycopg 3 (with psycopg[pool] / psycopg-pool installed) and raises ImproperlyConfigured with psycopg2; rename test_connect_pool_setting_ignored_for_psycopg2 accordingly.
findings.first_evidence: docs/ref/databases.txt:270-271 -- This option requires ``psycopg[pool]`` or :pypi:`psycopg-pool` to be installed / and is ignored with ``psycopg2``.

residual_risks: Fork inheritance of the class-level pool: DatabaseWrapper._connection_pools is process-global, so a pool opened before a fork (gunicorn --preload / prefork workers after a startup query, or fork-mode parallel test workers if a custom system check queries the alias after the clones are made) is inherited as 'already open' with sockets shared between processes and no worker threads; setup_worker_connection() does not close it. Not raised as a finding: an offline probe showed the stock `check --database` run opens no PostgreSQL connection, so the parallel-runner path needs project-specific checks to trigger.

Threads that use the ORM and exit without connection.close()/close_old_connections() never call putconn(); psycopg_pool's getconn() docstring states this depletes the pool. With "pool": True the default max_size is 4, so four such threads permanently exhaust the alias until process restart, where previously the socket was simply closed on garbage collection. Not verifiable without a server.

Connect kwargs are captured once per alias: backends or settings code that vary credentials per connection through get_connection_params()/settings_dict (rotating passwords, short-lived auth tokens) will keep using the first values for every new pooled connection.

destroy_test_db(keepdb=True) skips _destroy_test_db(), so the pool is neither closed nor rebound when settings_dict["NAME"] is restored to the original name; later access in the same process still reaches the kept test database.

ConnectionPool is always called with a `check=` argument, which tests/requirements pins to psycopg-pool>=3.2.0; behavior with an older installed psycopg_pool was not checked (only 3.3.3 is available offline) and no minimum version is enforced or documented.

No PostgreSQL server was available: findings 1 and 2 were verified with the real psycopg_pool plus a fake connection class and by inspecting pool kwargs, not against a live database. close_pool()/pool property races under concurrent threads (KeyError between the membership test, lookup and del) were not exercised; they are reachable only from test infrastructure and the TIME_ZONE/USE_TZ setting_changed handler.
testing_gaps: No test combines OPTIONS['pool'] with OPTIONS['assume_role']; test_connect_role was moved to no_pool_connection(), which hides the configure-callback deadlock.
No test covers autocommit disabled + connection.close() inside atomic() followed by reuse of the connection, the path the new ensure_connection() guard breaks on all backends.
No test asserts that a pooled alias follows a settings_dict NAME change (create_test_db, setup_worker_connection, set_as_test_mirror) after a connection was already opened on that alias.

findings.title: Base ensure_connection() guard permanently blocks reconnect when AUTOCOMMIT is False
findings.suggested_fix: In django/db/transaction.py Atomic.__exit__ (the `elif not connection.savepoint_ids and not connection.commit_on_exit:` branch, lines 309-313), reset the flag on both paths: `if connection.closed_in_transaction: connection.connection = None` followed unconditionally by `connection.in_atomic_block = False`, so the wrapper is no longer 'in an atomic block' once the outermost block has exited. Add a regression test in tests/transactions (file-backed or server DB, AUTOCOMMIT=False): open atomic, connection.close() inside it, exit, then assert a new cursor works. Assumption: the guard is only meant to fire while an atomic block is still open.

findings.title: PostgreSQL DatabaseWrapper.ensure_role() removed; timezone/role override hooks bypassed
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the module-level ensure_timezone()/ensure_role() functions with overridable instance methods that take the raw connection, e.g. `_configure_timezone(self, connection)` and `_configure_role(self, connection)`, have `_configure_connection()` call `self._configure_timezone(connection)` / `self._configure_role(connection)`, have `ensure_timezone()` delegate to `self._configure_timezone(self.connection)`, and restore `def ensure_role(self): return self._configure_role(self.connection)`. If dropping ensure_role() is intentional, add a note under 'Database backend API' in docs/releases/5.1.txt instead. Assumption: subclass overrides of these hooks are meant to keep working, as they did before this change.

findings.title: Docs say pool option is ignored with psycopg2; code raises
findings.suggested_fix: Change docs/ref/databases.txt:270-271 to state the real behaviour, e.g. "This option requires ``psycopg[pool]`` or :pypi:`psycopg-pool` to be installed and is not supported with ``psycopg2`` (an ``ImproperlyConfigured`` exception is raised).", and rename tests/backends/postgresql/tests.py:349 to test_connect_pool_setting_not_supported_for_psycopg2. Assumption: raising is the intended behaviour, since the test asserts it.
findings.first_evidence: docs/ref/databases.txt:270-271 -- This option requires ``psycopg[pool]`` or :pypi:`psycopg-pool` to be installed / and is ignored with ``psycopg2``.

residual_risks: OPTIONS['pool'] is documented as 'a dict to be passed to ConnectionPool' with no reserved keys, but Django already passes kwargs, open, configure and check; supplying any of them (verified offline for all four) raises a bare TypeError 'ConnectionPool() got multiple values for keyword argument ...' from the pool property instead of ImproperlyConfigured, and there is no documented way to add a custom configure/check callback.

External-consumer completeness is grep-only: no in-repo subclass overrides ensure_timezone()/ensure_role(), so the impact of the removed/bypassed hooks on third-party PostgreSQL-derived backends (which cannot be inspected offline) is inferred from the public method surface, not observed.

Closing a pooled connection inside an atomic block now surfaces ProgrammingError from ensure_connection(), whereas the non-pooled path keeps the closed driver connection and surfaces InterfaceError on the next query; code that catches InterfaceError for 'connection already closed' will not catch the pooled variant. Not verified against a live server (none provisioned).
testing_gaps: No test covers the base-backend guard through a real atomic block: the only test (test_cannot_open_new_connection_in_atomic_block) sets in_atomic_block/closed_in_transaction by hand on PostgreSQL+psycopg3. A backend-agnostic test with AUTOCOMMIT=False that closes the connection inside atomic() and then issues a query after the block would have caught the stuck-wrapper regression.
No test asserts that a DatabaseWrapper subclass overriding ensure_timezone()/ensure_role() still has those overrides used by init_connection_state() (and by the pool's configure callback).

findings.title: Pool configure callback reaches back into the wrapper via ops (Information Leakage)
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the `ops` parameter from the module-level helpers so they depend only on the raw psycopg connection: pass the constant time-zone SQL string (or inline it) to ensure_timezone, and in ensure_role mogrify against the raw connection instead of ops.compose_sql (psycopg 3: `ClientCursor(connection).mogrify("SET ROLE %s", [role_name])`; psycopg2: `cursor.mogrify(...).decode()`), e.g. via a raw-connection helper next to `mogrify` in psycopg_any.py. Then build the pool's `configure` from captured values (`functools.partial(_configure_connection, timezone_name=self.timezone_name, role_name=...)` on a module-level function) rather than the bound method `self._configure_connection`, and delete the now-unneeded "do not access anything on self" comment. Add a pooled test with assume_role (test_connect_role currently forces pool=False). Assumption: SET ROLE with a mogrified literal on the raw connection is equivalent to the existing compose_sql output.

findings.title: pool property mixes enabled-check with pool creation
findings.suggested_fix: Split the two concerns: keep `pool` as the lazy getter, and make teardown not go through it: `def close_pool(self): pool = self._connection_pools.pop(self.alias, None); if pool: pool.close()`. In get_new_connection bind once (`pool = self.pool; if pool: pool.open(); connection = pool.getconn()`). For the pure predicates in _close, init_connection_state and close_if_health_check_failed, either bind `self.pool` once per call or add a settings-only helper (e.g. `_is_pool_enabled` returning `self.alias != NO_DB_ALIAS and bool(self.settings_dict["OPTIONS"].get("pool"))`).

findings.title: Docs and test name say pool is ignored on psycopg2; code raises
findings.suggested_fix: Assuming the raise is the intended behaviour (it is what the test asserts): change the docs sentence to state that the option requires psycopg 3 and that using it with psycopg2 raises ImproperlyConfigured, and rename the test to e.g. test_connect_pool_setting_rejected_for_psycopg2. If ignoring was intended instead, delete the raise in get_connection_params() and make the test assert a normal connection.
findings.first_evidence: docs/ref/databases.txt:270-271 -- This option requires ``psycopg[pool]`` or :pypi:`psycopg-pool` to be installed\nand is ignored with ``psycopg2``.

findings.title: _close depends on psycopg private _pool as a test workaround
findings.suggested_fix: Have the wrapper remember the pool it borrowed from instead of reading psycopg's private attribute: in get_new_connection, bind `pool = self.pool`, call `pool.open()` / `pool.getconn()`, and store it (e.g. `self._connection_pool = pool`); in _close, return the connection with `self._connection_pool.putconn(self.connection)` and clear both references. This keeps the pool-swap-in-tests case working without `self.connection._pool`.

residual_risks: The runtime failure mode of pool + assume_role (thread-sharing DatabaseError vs. a getconn() PoolTimeout) was not exercised because no PostgreSQL server is provisioned; only the call from the configure callback into DatabaseWrapper.cursor() was demonstrated offline with a mocked raw connection.

The diff removes the DatabaseWrapper.ensure_role() method and adds module-level ensure_timezone()/ensure_role() functions that share a name with the remaining ensure_timezone() method; no in-repo callers of the removed method remain (callsite completeness: grep-only), but third-party backends subclassing the PostgreSQL wrapper are not visible from this checkout.

findings.suggested_fix: State that the option requires psycopg 3 and raises ImproperlyConfigured with psycopg2.

findings.suggested_fix: Have close_pool() pop an existing pool from _connection_pools instead of going through the lazily-creating pool property.

findings.title: close_pool() evaluates the pool property twice and can KeyError on concurrent del
findings.suggested_fix: pool = self._connection_pools.pop(self.alias, None); if pool: pool.close()
